title: Minimise a failing input
description:
A fuzzer found an input that makes a parser fail. Write `minimise(input, fails)`, which shrinks it to a smaller input that still fails, by greedy single-character removal:

1. Try removing the character at position 0, then 1, then 2, and so on, of the current input.
2. As soon as removing one gives an input for which `fails` still returns true, keep that shorter input and **start again from position 0**.
3. When no single removal still fails, return the current input.

`fails(input)` is guaranteed to be true for the original input. Also return how many times `fails` was called, so the cost can be compared with smarter methods.

```
fails = "contains both 'x' and 'y'"
minimise("abxcdye") -> "xy"
```
hints: Loop until a full pass over the positions removes nothing. In each pass, build a copy with one character removed and test it.
When a removal still fails, keep it and break out of the pass, so the next pass starts from position 0 of the new, shorter input.
